title.narrative: Evaluating the impact of long-term field projects and anti-poaching patrols on local populations of bonobos: a bottom-up approach for evidence based bonobo conservation

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to evaluate the population density of bonobos and other wildlife, monitor the status of human encroachment activities, and with this information, develop a conservation strategy for bonobos in a forest area of the buffer zone of Salonga National Park. The recipient will assess the population density of bonobos and other wildlife in a region of about 500 km2 that is assumed to vary in terms of the indirect and direct protection that it received over the last ten years from a long-term field project (LTFP) and from anti-poaching patrols (APP) in forests outside the study site; evaluate the frequency and nature of human encroachment within the 500 km2 in relation to the distance from the LTFP site and to the range covered by APP activities conducted over the past 3 years; and model the impact of the LTFP and APP activities on the local bonobo population in order to develop an evidence based conservation strategy.
